title: Algebraically closed field extensions with any prescribed cardinal lower bound
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $k$ be a $\mathcal U$-small field [def-weil-field] and let $\lambda$ be an infinite cardinal in $\mathcal U$. There exists a $\mathcal U$-small algebraically closed field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-algebraic-closure] with $\lambda\leq |K|$. The extension $K/k$ is not required to be algebraic.

source.place: Tag 09GT (theorem-existence-algebraic-closure), used after adjoining a set of independent variables and taking the fraction field. Agent cardinal-enlargement consequence; the construction is explained in the delivery report, not asserted to be the literal statement of 09GT.

proof.text:
Choose a $\mathcal U$-small set $I$ with $|I|=\lambda$, and form $R=k[x_i:i\in I]$ using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. A field is a domain: if $ab=0$ and $a
e0$, multiplication by $a^{-1}$ gives $b=0$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain] makes $R$ a domain. The coefficient of the monomial $x_i$ in $x_i$ is $1$, whereas in $x_j$ for $j
e i$ it is $0$; since $1
e0$, $i\mapsto x_i$ is injective. The constant-polynomial map $k	o R$ is injective by its coefficient at the constant monomial. The set $R$ is $\mathcal U$-small: its elements are finite coefficient-supported families on finite-support exponent families on $I$.

source.place: Tag 09FJ (example-quotient-field) followed by Tag 09GT (theorem-existence-algebraic-closure); agent cardinal-enlargement argument.

proof.text: Use the localization construction in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] with $B=R$, base ring $k$ and multiplicative subset $S=R\setminus\{0\}$. Set $F=S^{-1}R$. Its equality criterion reduces to $a/s=b/t$ iff $at=bs$, because $R$ is a domain and every multiplier in $S$ is nonzero. Hence $R\to F$, $a\mapsto a/1$, is injective, and $0\ne1$ in $F$. A nonzero $a/s$ has $a\ne0$ and inverse $s/a$, so $F$ is a field. The composite $k\to R\to F$ is a unital ring map and is injective. The fractions form a quotient of the $\mathcal U$-small set $R\times S$, so $F$ is $\mathcal U$-small. No finite-type assertion from the cited definition is used.

source.place: Tag 09FJ (example-quotient-field): quotient construction, cross-multiplication and inverse of a nonzero fraction.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique] to the field $F$, choosing an algebraic closure $K/F$. Apply this existence theorem inside $\mathcal U$: its construction is available in the same universe as $F$ (concretely, Mathlib's $\operatorname{AlgebraicClosure}(F)$ is defined in that universe). Thus $K$ is $\mathcal U$-small and algebraically closed. The field map $F\to K$ is injective by [def-pc-field-extension]. Composing $k\to F\to K$ equips $K$ with the required field extension of $k$.

The composite $I\to R\to F\to K$ is injective: equality in $K$ implies equality in $F$, then in $R$, and then equality of indices by step 1. It witnesses $\lambda=|I|\leq|K|$. The construction only requires $K/F$ to be algebraic; it imposes no algebraicity condition on $K/k$, as required.
